page_title: Remove Objects & People from Photos: Free AI Inpainting | wipe.photos

sources.entry: Wipe - Remove people and objects from photos entirely in your browser. No upload, no signup, no watermark. #free

summary.name: wipe.photos
summary.one_liner: A free browser-based AI tool that removes unwanted objects, people, text, and logos from photos by painting over them and letting AI inpaint the background.
use_cases: Removing a stranger or photobomber from a vacation photo
Erasing text, signs, or logos from an image
Cleaning up power lines or stray objects in landscape shots
Editing photos privately without uploading them to a server
Quick touch-ups on a phone or laptop browser
summary.what_it_does: The user uploads a JPG, PNG, or WebP photo, paints over the object, person, or text to remove, and the AI fills the area with reconstructed background. The result downloads as a PNG. The editing runs entirely in the browser using the LaMa (Large Mask inpainting) model via onnxruntime-web, so photos are said not to leave the device. It uses WebGPU for acceleration when available, and the first visit downloads the model once for local storage. The page says results depend on the background, working best on fabric, grass, pavement, and walls.
notable: Runs entirely in the browser; photos are not uploaded to a server
Uses LaMa inpainting model by Samsung Research, Apache 2.0 licensed, served as the project's own ONNX conversion of big-lama
No signup, no watermark, no usage cap stated
WebGPU acceleration; under 1 second on an M3 MacBook with Chrome per the page
caveats: Results depend heavily on the background; complex backgrounds may fare worse
Accepts only JPG, PNG, and WebP input; output is PNG
Requires JavaScript; first visit downloads the model
Performance is faster with a GPU and Chrome, though not required
